name: Cabo Verde
headline: Cabo Verde: +6.3% growth in 2025, 2.3% inflation, debt 115% of GDP
sections: Cabo Verde is a $3.1 billion economy (2025), the world's 185th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +6.3% in 2025, faster than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $12K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 5.2% of GDP (2025).

Consumer prices rose 2.3% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 7.9% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 8.5% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 28.4% (2025).
Gross government debt is 115% of GDP (2025), a very high level that has fallen from 168% in 2020. The general government balance is +1.1% of GDP (2025), a surplus.
The current account balance is +3.4% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 95% of GDP (2025), a fairly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 5.0% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 81% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 76.2 years (2024). Population: 514 thousand (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
